title: Xiongnu
note: Steppe empire centred on Mongolia, c. 209 BCE to the late 1st century CE (Lee et al. 2023, Science Advances, PMC10104459, opened). Han accounts are hostile outsiders' views; centre archaeology and aDNA (Egiin Gol, Takhiltyn Khotgor, Shombuuzyn Belchir elite women's burials). Primary region is Mongolia, which the M49 list folds into eastern_asia; decide and justify.

title: Zhang Qian
note: Life path Chang'an – Xiongnu captivity – Ferghana – Sogdiana – Bactria – return c. 13 years later; marquis of Bowang 123 BCE; tomb at Chenggu, Hanzhong (UNESCO 1442 component, N33 09 32 E107 17 28). Hirth 1917 translation on Silk Road Seattle; Shiji 123 / Hanshu 61. Birth year unknown: use death c. 114 BCE only if sourced. His Xiongnu wife and companion Gan Fu deserve mention.

title: Cai Lun presents improved papermaking to the Han court
note: Hou Hanshu 78 (Yuanxing 1 = 105 CE; bark, hemp, rags, nets). Perspective: Western Han paper at Fangmatan (Gansu, c. 2nd c. BCE map fragment) and Xuanquan posthouse; dispute over whether these are true paper (Xinhua 2016, HK Museum of History 1998). Starts the paper thread toward Samarkand (751 tradition) and Gutenberg. Find a peer-reviewed fibre-analysis paper.

title: Ban Zhao
note: Woman historian and court scholar who completed parts of the Hanshu after her brother Ban Gu's death and wrote Lessons for Women (Nüjie). Under-recorded woman; sources thin online — look for university-press translations (Nancy Lee Swann 1932) and Hou Hanshu 84 Biographies of Women. Dates c. 45–c. 117 CE need sourcing.

title: Yellow Turban Rebellion
note: Hou Hanshu 8: Zhonghe 1, 2nd month, Zhang Jue of Julu, followers claimed 360,000, simultaneous rising; He Jin appointed. Religious movement (Way of Great Peace) as belief; casualties unknown — say so. Loewe (CHC 1) treats it as the real end of Han authority. Needs audience_note.

title: Han conquest of Nanyue and the commanderies of northern Vietnam
note: Emperor Wu's annexation of the Nanyue kingdom (capital Panyu, modern Guangzhou; Nanyue King's tomb museum) and the commanderies of Jiaozhi, Jiuzhen and Rinan; later Trưng sisters' rising (40–43 CE) as a linked Vietnamese-centred target. Verify 111 BCE date; South-East Asia is under-covered.
